pr_title: DEPR: _BaseOffset's parameter `n` should be prevented from being 0
pr_body:
- [ ] closes #31184

pr_comments: I think @jbrockmendel has done similar work on these in the past
Are we sure this should be enforced for _all_ (non-tick) DateOffset subclasses?  `Week` comes to mind as a possible exception.

@jbrockmendel As I noted on the issue, n=0 is currently docced as a rollforward for the general DateOffset class, although it's suggested that "since 0 is a bit weird, we suggest avoiding its use". Perhaps the first step should be officially deprecating n=0 DateOffsets before removal?

With Week, so far as I can tell Week(n=0) does absolutely nothing (not even a rollforward). Not sure whether that speaks in its favor (doing nothing for a 0 offset is unambiguous and in some sense logical) or against it (using it doesn't actually do anything)?

```python
In [3]: pd.to_datetime('2020-01-22') + pd.offsets.Week(n=0)
Out[3]: Timestamp('2020-01-22 00:00:00')

In [4]: pd.to_datetime('2020-01-22') + pd.offsets.Week(n=1)
Out[4]: Timestamp('2020-01-29 00:00:00')

In [5]: pd.to_datetime('2020-01-21') + pd.offsets.Week(n=0)
Out[5]: Timestamp('2020-01-21 00:00:00')

In [6]: pd.to_datetime('2020-01-21 01:29') + pd.offsets.Week(n=0)
Out[6]: Timestamp('2020-01-21 01:29:00')
```

> although it's suggested that "since 0 is a bit weird, we suggest avoiding its use". Perhaps the first step should be officially deprecating n=0 DateOffsets before removal?

I think this makes sense, cc @jreback @mroeschke 

> With Week, so far as I can tell Week(n=0) does absolutely nothing (not even a rollforward).

`Week(n=whatever, normalize=False, weekday=None)` is equivalent to `Day(n=7*whatever)`.  It's kind of annoying to have that one tick-like non-Tick.  Could deprecate the weekday=None option (I'm getting off topic)

@jbrockmendel Sorry, having some trouble with this one.

I've added a FutureWarning to `_validate_n` from `pandas/_libs/tslibs/offsets.pyx::_BaseOffset`, re-ran
```
$ python setup.py develop
```

```

```
to `_check_offsetfunc_works` from `pandas/tests/tseries/offsets/test_offsets.py::TestCommon`.

However, when I run
```
$ pytest pandas/tests/tseries/offsets/test_offsets.py::TestCommon::test_apply
```
I still get
```
AssertionError: Caused unexpected warning(s): [('FutureWarning', FutureWarning('Deprecated n=0'), '/home/SERILOCAL/m.gorelli/pandas/pandas/tseries/offsets.py', 1290)]
```

(note: I'm aware that "Deprecated n=0" isn't an adequate warning message, I just wanted to try getting this working before looking into how to write the message properly)

@jbrockmendel sorry to tag you here again, just don't know what to make of the CI failure. If I run 
```
$ python setup.py develop
$ pytest pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_numeric.py
```
locally on Linux, Python 3.7.6, it passes. But during the "Linux py37_np_dev" CI job, this test fails.

Any suggestions on why this may be would be appreciated, else I'll keep trying to figure it out :)

> Instead, use with tm.assert_produces_warning(FutureWarning):

Just a note on this: the part of the code where I wanted to apply this (pandas/tests/tseries/offsets/test_offsets.py, line 367) doesn't always produce a ``FutureWarning``, so I wanted to just ignore the warning. Have used ``warnings.filterwarnings``

Found it, I need to run the tests with the `-W error` flag
It looks like the n!=0 restriction is being applied to offsets.Second, when it shouldn't apply to any of the Tick offsets.

issue_context.title: _BaseOffset's parameter `n` should be prevented from being 0
issue_context.body:
The docstring says
```
        Require that `n` be a nonzero integer.
```
but the "nonzero" condition isn't enforced.

Enforcing it would prevent the undesired behaviour noticed in #29901 , whereby
```
cbh = pd.offsets.CustomBusinessHour(start='07:00', end='01:00')
time = pd.Timestamp('2019-03-06 13:00:00')
time + 0*cbh
```
was returning
```
2019-03-07 07:00:00
```
comments:
Offset 0 is still officially docced as a rollforward, see https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.tseries.offsets.DateOffset.html#pandas.tseries.offsets.DateOffset.

```
Zero presents a problem. Should it roll forward or back? We arbitrarily have it rollforward:
date + BDay(0) == BDay.rollforward(date)
Since 0 is a bit weird, we suggest avoiding its use.
```

This has been in the doc as "discouraged" for a long time, but has also been docced as the behavior of offset 0 since time immemorial. Does this need a deprecation in code or has the "discouraged" been in long enough that this can be considered already deprecated (in which case the doc needs to be updated)?
That's a good point, thanks - I'd imagine the core would want a deprecation warning first
I think determined in #31185 that n=0 needs to be allowed (lest `period - period` raise), so the doc should be updated
The docstring no longer says "nonzero".  closing.

review_comments: once this deprecation is enforced, what would happen here?  just not-allowing subtraction seems undesirable

Yes, true that it seems undesirable. Any suggestions? I thought of returning an offset that allows for `n=0`, but that could be undesirable if other time arithmetic operations are involved.

For reference, when we get here, we have
```python
ipdb> idx                                                                                                                                     
PeriodIndex(['2011-01', '2011-02', '2011-03', '2011-04'], dtype='period[M]', name='idx', freq='M')
```
Looking back at #31184 wouldnt removing the incorrect doc also be a viable option?
LOL yeah, that would be a lot simpler :) Perhaps there could still be a warning that an offset with `n=0` has been created - what do you think?
could the warning go closer to the problematic behavior?
maybe do this in compat or tm?
